thread_analysis.thread_summary: Single-message thread (with a long nested quote chain covering the full history) for a customer (internal contact: [PERSON], via ACCESS/Phoenix Engineering referral) completing Bluetooth registration for a module-based product. The chain covers the full sales-to-registration lifecycle: RF/RF PHY test exemption determination (module has antenna connector), ICS-based profile test exemption logic for A2DP/AVRCP/DI, a new-customer pre-payment requirement and the resulting lead-time schedule, and the post-registration Compliance Folder requirement (including what substitutes for a missing operation manual on a non-publicly-sold product). Registration was completed and the SDoC confirmation was issued; Compliance Folder creation was still pending submission of supporting documents.
all_questions_found: Is the Compliance Folder required for a product not sold publicly?
No operation manual exists — what can substitute for it in the Compliance Folder?
What does 'ICS support' mean, and does keeping the Bluetooth stack unchanged exempt the product from profile testing for A2DP/AVRCP/DI?
Is RF/RF PHY testing required for this product, given the Bluetooth module's antenna connector?

Since there is no prior transaction history between the companies, can payment be made after wire transfer is sent (i.e., is pre-payment required), and what is the resulting delivery/lead-time schedule?
Is the Contact Person / contact information field required on the registration request form?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: RF/RF PHY testing was exempted because the customer's module datasheet showed it has an antenna connector (a standard module-level exemption path). Separately, profile testing for A2DP/AVRCP/DI is exempted if the product's ICS (Implementation Conformance Statement) support matches, or is a subset of, the ICS support already declared for the reference Bluetooth host stack D063309 (Fluoride Bluetooth Host Subsystem) — the consultant explained that ICS is a SIG-defined document breaking down each profile/protocol into minimal supported-feature items (YES/NO), and since the customer was not modifying the Bluetooth stack, the existing ICS declaration carried over and no product-level profile test was required. The Compliance Folder requirement (QPRDv3) is unconditional regardless of sales channel; for this non-publicly-sold (B2B) product lacking a consumer operation manual, product specifications/engineering documents (already prepared for the product's separate Japan Radio Law construction-type certification) were accepted as substitutes for the operation manual, block diagram, outline drawing, and antenna data components of the folder.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: (1) RF/RF PHY exemption: module with antenna connector, per datasheet review, is exempt. (2) Profile test exemption: compare the product's ICS support declaration against the pre-certified host stack's (D063309) ICS support — if equal or a subset, and the stack itself is unmodified, profile testing is exempted. (3) New customer with no transaction history: standard practice is pre-payment (work begins only after the customer's wire transfer is sent), and the quoted ~1 month total lead time runs from payment date through wire transfer to SIG (~3 weeks), proxy registration (1-3 business days), and Compliance Folder creation (1-3 business days after the customer submits required documents). (4) Compliance Folder is unconditional under QPRDv3; missing operation manual can be substituted with specs/engineering docs, often reusable from the product's other regulatory certification efforts.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Skipping the Compliance Folder for a non-publicly-sold product is still a QPRDv3 violation; SIG may revoke the qualification if the Compliance Folder cannot be produced on request. Misapplying the ICS comparison (e.g., approving profile-test exemption when the customer's ICS support actually exceeds the reference stack's declared support) would result in an unqualified product being registered as qualified. Not clarifying the pre-payment requirement and lead-time chain up front with a new customer can cause scheduling disputes.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When customers say 'our product is not publicly sold so we don't have a manual' — this is a predictable objection. Prepare a standard response: 'QPRDv3 requires a Compliance Folder for all registrations. For your product, product specifications or engineering documents can replace the operation manual.' Separately, when a customer asks about 'ICS support' terminology, explain it concretely (SIG-defined per-feature YES/NO declaration document) and tie the profile-test exemption decision directly to whether the customer's ICS support matches or is a subset of the pre-certified reference stack's ICS, with no modification to the stack itself. For new customers with no transaction history, state the pre-payment requirement and full lead-time chain explicitly and early to avoid timeline disputes.
